== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Incarnations are powerful entities that represent the essence and nature of specific Territories. They typically originate when a [[Traveler]] draws excessive power from their [[Territory]] into themselves, upsetting the natural balance and causing them to become an embodiment of that realm's power. This process often results in the [[Traveler]] losing control and becoming a force of nature, similar to gravity or heat. While they are sometimes viewed with dread as monsters that spread chaos and madness, they are not inherently evil; rather, they act according to the specific characteristics of their home [[Territory]]. For example, an [[Incarnation]] might seek combat, spread emotional energy, or pursue knowledge, depending on its origin. These beings possess the ability to warp reality around them, reshaping the environment to mirror their home [[Territory]]. However, this connection also acts as a tether, as Incarnations are meant to exist only within their own realms and can become trapped if they remain in a [[Territory]] for too long. Historically, the kingdom of [[Damasca]] has maintained security by using a [[ritual]] involving [[blood]] sacrifices to the [[Trees]] to keep these entities sealed away. When the seals are weakened or broken, Incarnations can pose a significant threat to the world, though they may eventually fade away after being returned to their respective Territories.}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Incarnations are noble, immensely powerful entities that were once imprisoned and are feared as monsters capable of spreading chaos and madness. These beings, which [[Alin]] believes should never have been released by the people of [[Enosh]], are essentially a [[Traveler]]'s power that has gone rampant. Because they go mad if they remain in the world for too long, they risk becoming trapped within the Territories that originally created them. Following the escape of an [[Incarnation]] from [[Valinhall]], its rampage highlights a threat that could potentially unseat the power of [[Talos]]'s father.}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">8</span></div>
<ul class="wv-fact-list mw-collapsible-content">

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|[[Incarnations]] are noble creatures with incalculable power that go mad if they stay in the world too long.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c6" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|An [[Incarnation]] from [[Valinhall]] has escaped and is on a rampage.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c7">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 7</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|[[Incarnations]] become trapped if they stay too long in the Territories that created them.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c8">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 8</ref>}}</li>

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The emergence of the [[Incarnations]] could unseat the power of [[Talos]]'s father.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c16">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 16</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|[[Incarnations]] are beings that the people of [[Enosh]] released.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c17">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 17</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The [[Incarnations]] are a group that [[Alin]] believes should not be released.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c22">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 22</ref>}}</li>

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|When unbound, Incarnations act according to their inherent nature and are notoriously lacking in self-control. Described as walking natural disasters, some of these entities are little better than monsters that can withstand attacks from [[Travelers]] without even paying attention. At least eight of the original nine were lured into transforming outside of a [[Territory]], and they utilized illusions, phantom noises, and physical abuse to torment [[Indirial]]. While [[Simon]] possesses the ability to prevent them from harming ordinary people, [[Caela]] noted that the Incarnations were not present on the battlefield.}}
